506	    /// Parse a single CSV field in `input` and copy field data to `output`.
507	    ///
508	    /// This routine requires a caller provided buffer of CSV data as the
509	    /// `input` and a caller provided buffer, `output`, in which to store field
510	    /// data extracted from `input`. The field data copied to `output` will
511	    /// have its quotes unescaped.
512	    ///
513	    /// Calling this routine parses at most a single field and returns
514	    /// three values indicating the state of the parser. The first value, a
515	    /// `ReadFieldResult`, tells the caller what to do next. For example, if
516	    /// the entire input was read or if the output buffer was filled before
517	    /// a full field had been read, then `ReadFieldResult::InputEmpty` or
518	    /// `ReadFieldResult::OutputFull` is returned, respectively. See the
519	    /// documentation for `ReadFieldResult` for more details.
520	    ///
521	    /// The other two values returned correspond to the number of bytes
522	    /// read from `input` and written to `output`, respectively.
523	    ///
524	    /// # Termination
525	    ///
526	    /// This reader interprets an empty `input` buffer as an indication that
527	    /// there is no CSV data left to read. Namely, when the caller has
528	    /// exhausted all CSV data, the caller should continue to call `read` with
529	    /// an empty input buffer until `ReadFieldResult::End` is returned.
530	    ///
531	    /// # Errors
532	    ///
533	    /// This CSV reader can never return an error. Instead, it prefers *a*
534	    /// parse over *no* parse.
535	    pub fn read_field(
536	        &mut self,
537	        input: &[u8],
538	        output: &mut [u8],
539	    ) -> (ReadFieldResult, usize, usize) {
540	        let (input, bom_nin) = self.strip_utf8_bom(input);
541	        let (res, nin, nout) = if self.use_nfa {
542	            self.read_field_nfa(input, output)
543	        } else {
544	            self.read_field_dfa(input, output)
545	        };
546	        self.has_read = true;
547	        (res, nin + bom_nin, nout)
548	    }

550	    /// Parse a single CSV record in `input` and copy each field contiguously
551	    /// to `output`, with the end position of each field written to `ends`.
552	    ///
553	    /// **NOTE**: This method is more cumbersome to use than `read_field`, but
554	    /// it can be faster since it amortizes more work.
555	    ///
556	    /// This routine requires a caller provided buffer of CSV data as the
557	    /// `input` and two caller provided buffers to store the unescaped field
558	    /// data (`output`) and the end position of each field in the record
559	    /// (`fields`).
560	    ///
561	    /// Calling this routine parses at most a single record and returns four
562	    /// values indicating the state of the parser. The first value, a
563	    /// `ReadRecordResult`, tells the caller what to do next. For example, if
564	    /// the entire input was read or if the output buffer was filled before a
565	    /// full field had been read, then `ReadRecordResult::InputEmpty` or
566	    /// `ReadRecordResult::OutputFull` is returned, respectively. Similarly, if
567	    /// the `ends` buffer is full, then `ReadRecordResult::OutputEndsFull` is
568	    /// returned. See the documentation for `ReadRecordResult` for more
569	    /// details.
570	    ///
571	    /// The other three values correspond to the number of bytes read from
572	    /// `input`, the number of bytes written to `output` and the number of
573	    /// end positions written to `ends`, respectively.
574	    ///
575	    /// The end positions written to `ends` are constructed as if there was
576	    /// a single contiguous buffer in memory containing the entire row, even
577	    /// if `ReadRecordResult::OutputFull` was returned in the middle of reading
578	    /// a row.
579	    ///
580	    /// # Termination
581	    ///
582	    /// This reader interprets an empty `input` buffer as an indication that
583	    /// there is no CSV data left to read. Namely, when the caller has
584	    /// exhausted all CSV data, the caller should continue to call `read` with
585	    /// an empty input buffer until `ReadRecordResult::End` is returned.
586	    ///
587	    /// # Errors
588	    ///
589	    /// This CSV reader can never return an error. Instead, it prefers *a*
590	    /// parse over *no* parse.
591	    pub fn read_record(
592	        &mut self,
593	        input: &[u8],
594	        output: &mut [u8],
595	        ends: &mut [usize],
596	    ) -> (ReadRecordResult, usize, usize, usize) {
597	        let (input, bom_nin) = self.strip_utf8_bom(input);
598	        let (res, nin, nout, nend) = if self.use_nfa {
599	            self.read_record_nfa(input, output, ends)
600	        } else {
601	            self.read_record_dfa(input, output, ends)
602	        };
603	        self.has_read = true;
604	        (res, nin + bom_nin, nout, nend)
605	    }

607	    /// Strip off a possible UTF-8 BOM at the start of a file. Quick note that
608	    /// this method will fail to strip off the BOM if only part of the BOM is
609	    /// buffered. Hopefully that won't happen very often.
610	    fn strip_utf8_bom<'a>(&self, input: &'a [u8]) -> (&'a [u8], usize) {
611	        if !self.has_read
612	            && input.len() >= 3
613	            && &input[0..3] == b"\xef\xbb\xbf"
614	        {
615	            (&input[3..], 3)
616	        } else {
617	            (input, 0)
618	        }
619	    }
620	
621	    #[inline(always)]
622	    fn read_record_dfa(
623	        &mut self,
624	        input: &[u8],
625	        output: &mut [u8],
626	        ends: &mut [usize],
627	    ) -> (ReadRecordResult, usize, usize, usize) {
628	        if input.is_empty() {
629	            let s = self.transition_final_dfa(self.dfa_state);
630	            let res =
631	                self.dfa.new_read_record_result(s, true, false, false, false);
632	            // This part is a little tricky. When reading the final record,
633	            // the last result the caller will get is an InputEmpty, and while
634	            // they'll have everything they need in `output`, they'll be
635	            // missing the final end position of the final field in `ends`.
636	            // We insert that here, but we must take care to handle the case
637	            // where `ends` doesn't have enough space. If it doesn't have
638	            // enough space, then we also can't transition to the next state.
639	            return match res {
640	                ReadRecordResult::Record => {
641	                    if ends.is_empty() {
642	                        return (ReadRecordResult::OutputEndsFull, 0, 0, 0);
643	                    }
644	                    self.dfa_state = s;
645	                    ends[0] = self.output_pos;
646	                    self.output_pos = 0;
647	                    (res, 0, 0, 1)
648	                }
649	                _ => {
650	                    self.dfa_state = s;
651	                    (res, 0, 0, 0)
652	                }
653	            };
654	        }
655	        if output.is_empty() {
656	            return (ReadRecordResult::OutputFull, 0, 0, 0);
657	        }
658	        if ends.is_empty() {
659	            return (ReadRecordResult::OutputEndsFull, 0, 0, 0);
660	        }
661	        let (mut nin, mut nout, mut nend) = (0, 0, 0);
662	        let mut state = self.dfa_state;
663	        while nin < input.len() && nout < output.len() && nend < ends.len() {
664	            let (s, has_out) = self.dfa.get_output(state, input[nin]);
665	            self.line += (input[nin] == b'\n') as u64;
666	            state = s;
667	            if has_out {
668	                output[nout] = input[nin];
669	                nout += 1;
670	            }
671	            nin += 1;
672	            if state >= self.dfa.final_field {
673	                ends[nend] = self.output_pos + nout;
674	                nend += 1;
675	                if state > self.dfa.final_field {
676	                    break;
677	                }
678	            }
679	            if state == self.dfa.in_field || state == self.dfa.in_quoted {
680	                self.dfa
681	                    .classes
682	                    .scan_and_copy(input, &mut nin, output, &mut nout);
683	            }
684	        }
685	        let res = self.dfa.new_read_record_result(
686	            state,
687	            false,
688	            nin >= input.len(),
689	            nout >= output.len(),
690	            nend >= ends.len(),
691	        );
692	        self.dfa_state = state;
693	        if res.is_record() {
694	            self.output_pos = 0;
695	        } else {
696	            self.output_pos += nout;
697	        }
698	        (res, nin, nout, nend)
699	    }

701	    #[inline(always)]
702	    fn read_field_dfa(
703	        &mut self,
704	        input: &[u8],
705	        output: &mut [u8],
706	    ) -> (ReadFieldResult, usize, usize) {
707	        if input.is_empty() {
708	            self.dfa_state = self.transition_final_dfa(self.dfa_state);
709	            let res = self.dfa.new_read_field_result(
710	                self.dfa_state,
711	                true,
712	                false,
713	                false,
714	            );
715	            return (res, 0, 0);
716	        }
717	        if output.is_empty() {
718	            return (ReadFieldResult::OutputFull, 0, 0);
719	        }
720	        let (mut nin, mut nout) = (0, 0);
721	        let mut state = self.dfa_state;
722	        while nin < input.len() && nout < output.len() {
723	            let b = input[nin];
724	            self.line += (b == b'\n') as u64;
725	            let (s, has_out) = self.dfa.get_output(state, b);
726	            state = s;
727	            if has_out {
728	                output[nout] = b;
729	                nout += 1;
730	            }
731	            nin += 1;
732	            if state >= self.dfa.final_field {
733	                break;
734	            }
735	        }
736	        let res = self.dfa.new_read_field_result(
737	            state,
738	            false,
739	            nin >= input.len(),
740	            nout >= output.len(),
741	        );
742	        self.dfa_state = state;
743	        (res, nin, nout)
744	    }

746	    /// Perform the final state transition, i.e., when the caller indicates
747	    /// that the input has been exhausted.
748	    fn transition_final_dfa(&self, state: DfaState) -> DfaState {
749	        // If we''ve already emitted a record or think we're ready to start
750	        // parsing a new record, then we should sink into the final state
751	        // and never move from there. (pro-tip: the start state doubles as
752	        // the final state!)
753	        if state >= self.dfa.final_record || state.is_start() {
754	            self.dfa.new_state_final_end()
755	        } else {
756	            self.dfa.new_state_final_record()
757	        }
758	    }

760	    /// Write the transition tables for the DFA based on this parser's
761	    /// configuration.
762	    fn build_dfa(&mut self) {
763	        // A naive DFA transition table has
764	        // `cells = (# number of states) * (# size of alphabet)`. While we
765	        // could get away with that, the table would have `10 * 256 = 2560`
766	        // entries. Even worse, in order to avoid a multiplication instruction
767	        // when computing the next transition, we store the starting index of
768	        // each state's row, which would not be representible in a single byte.
769	        // So we'd need a `u16`, which doubles our transition table size to
770	        // ~5KB. This is a lot to put on the stack, even though it probably
771	        // fits in the L1 cache of most modern CPUs.
772	        //
773	        // To avoid this, we note that while our "true" alphabet
774	        // has 256 distinct possibilities, the DFA itself is only
775	        // discriminatory on a very small subset of that alphabet. For
776	        // example, assuming neither `a` nor `b` are set as special
777	        // quote/comment/escape/delimiter/terminator bytes, they are otherwise
778	        // indistinguishable to the DFA, so it would be OK to treat them as
779	        // if they were equivalent. That is, they are in the same equivalence
780	        // class.
781	        //
782	        // As it turns out, using this logic, we can shrink our effective
783	        // alphabet down to 7 equivalence classes:
784	        //
785	        //   1. The field delimiter.
786	        //   2. The record terminator.
787	        //   3. If the record terminator is CRLF, then CR and LF are
788	        //      distinct equivalence classes.
789	        //   4. The quote byte.
790	        //   5. The escape byte.
791	        //   6. The comment byte.
792	        //   7. Everything else.
793	        //
794	        // We add those equivalence classes here. If more configuration knobs
795	        // are added to the parser with more discriminating bytes, then this
796	        // logic will need to be adjusted further.
797	        //
798	        // Even though this requires an extra bit of indirection when computing
799	        // the next transition, microbenchmarks say that it doesn't make much
800	        // of a difference. Perhaps because everything fits into the L1 cache.
801	        self.dfa.classes.add(self.delimiter);
802	        if self.quoting {
803	            self.dfa.classes.add(self.quote);
804	            if let Some(escape) = self.escape {
805	                self.dfa.classes.add(escape);
806	            }
807	        }
808	        if let Some(comment) = self.comment {
809	            self.dfa.classes.add(comment);
810	        }
811	        match self.term {
812	            Terminator::Any(b) => self.dfa.classes.add(b),
813	            Terminator::CRLF => {
814	                self.dfa.classes.add(b'\r');
815	                self.dfa.classes.add(b'\n');
816	            }
817	        }
818	        // Build the DFA transition table by computing the DFA state for all
819	        // possible combinations of state and input byte.
820	        for &state in NFA_STATES {
821	            for c in (0..256).map(|c| c as u8) {
822	                let mut nfa_result = (state, NfaInputAction::Epsilon);
823	                // Consume NFA states until we hit a non-epsilon transition.
824	                while nfa_result.0 != NfaState::End
825	                    && nfa_result.1 == NfaInputAction::Epsilon
826	                {
827	                    nfa_result = self.transition_nfa(nfa_result.0, c);
828	                }
829	                let from = self.dfa.new_state(state);
830	                let to = self.dfa.new_state(nfa_result.0);
831	                self.dfa.set(
832	                    from,
833	                    c,
834	                    to,
835	                    nfa_result.1 == NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput,
836	                );
837	            }
838	        }
839	        self.dfa_state = self.dfa.new_state(NfaState::StartRecord);
840	        self.dfa.finish();
841	    }
842	
843	    // The NFA implementation follows. The transition_final_nfa and
844	    // transition_nfa methods are required for the DFA to operate. The
845	    // rest are included for completeness (and debugging). Note that this
846	    // NFA implementation is included in most of the CSV parser tests below.
847	
848	    #[inline(always)]
849	    fn read_record_nfa(
850	        &mut self,
851	        input: &[u8],
852	        output: &mut [u8],
853	        ends: &mut [usize],
854	    ) -> (ReadRecordResult, usize, usize, usize) {
855	        if input.is_empty() {
856	            let s = self.transition_final_nfa(self.nfa_state);
857	            let res = ReadRecordResult::from_nfa(s, false, false, false);
858	            return match res {
859	                ReadRecordResult::Record => {
860	                    if ends.is_empty() {
861	                        return (ReadRecordResult::OutputEndsFull, 0, 0, 0);
862	                    }
863	                    self.nfa_state = s;
864	                    ends[0] = self.output_pos;
865	                    self.output_pos = 0;
866	                    (res, 0, 0, 1)
867	                }
868	                _ => {
869	                    self.nfa_state = s;
870	                    (res, 0, 0, 0)
871	                }
872	            };
873	        }
874	        if output.is_empty() {
875	            return (ReadRecordResult::OutputFull, 0, 0, 0);
876	        }
877	        if ends.is_empty() {
878	            return (ReadRecordResult::OutputEndsFull, 0, 0, 0);
879	        }
880	        let (mut nin, mut nout, mut nend) = (0, self.output_pos, 0);
881	        let mut state = self.nfa_state;
882	        while nin < input.len() && nout < output.len() && nend < ends.len() {
883	            let (s, io) = self.transition_nfa(state, input[nin]);
884	            match io {
885	                NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput => {
886	                    output[nout] = input[nin];
887	                    nout += 1;
888	                    nin += 1;
889	                }
890	                NfaInputAction::Discard => {
891	                    nin += 1;
892	                }
893	                NfaInputAction::Epsilon => {}
894	            }
895	            state = s;
896	            if state.is_field_final() {
897	                ends[nend] = nout;
898	                nend += 1;
899	                if state != NfaState::EndFieldDelim {
900	                    break;
901	                }
902	            }
903	        }
904	        let res = ReadRecordResult::from_nfa(
905	            state,
906	            nin >= input.len(),
907	            nout >= output.len(),
908	            nend >= ends.len(),
909	        );
910	        self.nfa_state = state;
911	        self.output_pos = if res.is_record() { 0 } else { nout };
912	        (res, nin, nout, nend)
913	    }

915	    #[inline(always)]
916	    fn read_field_nfa(
917	        &mut self,
918	        input: &[u8],
919	        output: &mut [u8],
920	    ) -> (ReadFieldResult, usize, usize) {
921	        if input.is_empty() {
922	            self.nfa_state = self.transition_final_nfa(self.nfa_state);
923	            let res = ReadFieldResult::from_nfa(self.nfa_state, false, false);
924	            return (res, 0, 0);
925	        }
926	        if output.is_empty() {
927	            // If the output buffer is empty, then we can never make progress,
928	            // so just quit now.
929	            return (ReadFieldResult::OutputFull, 0, 0);
930	        }
931	        let (mut nin, mut nout) = (0, 0);
932	        let mut state = self.nfa_state;
933	        while nin < input.len() && nout < output.len() {
934	            let (s, io) = self.transition_nfa(state, input[nin]);
935	            match io {
936	                NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput => {
937	                    output[nout] = input[nin];
938	                    nout += 1;
939	                    nin += 1;
940	                }
941	                NfaInputAction::Discard => {
942	                    nin += 1;
943	                }
944	                NfaInputAction::Epsilon => (),
945	            }
946	            state = s;
947	            if state.is_field_final() {
948	                break;
949	            }
950	        }
951	        let res = ReadFieldResult::from_nfa(
952	            state,
953	            nin >= input.len(),
954	            nout >= output.len(),
955	        );
956	        self.nfa_state = state;
957	        (res, nin, nout)
958	    }

960	    /// Compute the final NFA transition after all caller-provided input has
961	    /// been exhausted.
962	    #[inline(always)]
963	    fn transition_final_nfa(&self, state: NfaState) -> NfaState {
964	        use self::NfaState::*;
965	        match state {
966	            End | StartRecord | EndRecord | InComment | CRLF => End,
967	            StartField | EndFieldDelim | EndFieldTerm | InField
968	            | InQuotedField | InEscapedQuote | InDoubleEscapedQuote
969	            | InRecordTerm => EndRecord,
970	        }
971	    }
972	
973	    /// Compute the next NFA state given the current NFA state and the current
974	    /// input byte.
975	    ///
976	    /// This returns the next NFA state along with an NfaInputAction that
977	    /// indicates what should be done with the input byte (nothing for an epsilon
978	    /// transition, copied to a caller provided output buffer, or discarded).
979	    #[inline(always)]
980	    fn transition_nfa(
981	        &self,
982	        state: NfaState,
983	        c: u8,
984	    ) -> (NfaState, NfaInputAction) {
985	        use self::NfaState::*;
986	        match state {
987	            End => (End, NfaInputAction::Epsilon),
988	            StartRecord => {
989	                if self.term.equals(c) {
990	                    (StartRecord, NfaInputAction::Discard)
991	                } else if self.comment == Some(c) {
992	                    (InComment, NfaInputAction::Discard)
993	                } else {
994	                    (StartField, NfaInputAction::Epsilon)
995	                }
996	            }
997	            EndRecord => (StartRecord, NfaInputAction::Epsilon),
998	            StartField => {
999	                if self.quoting && self.quote == c {
1000	                    (InQuotedField, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1001	                } else if self.delimiter == c {
1002	                    (EndFieldDelim, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1003	                } else if self.term.equals(c) {
1004	                    (EndFieldTerm, NfaInputAction::Epsilon)
1005	                } else {
1006	                    (InField, NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput)
1007	                }
1008	            }
1009	            EndFieldDelim => (StartField, NfaInputAction::Epsilon),
1010	            EndFieldTerm => (InRecordTerm, NfaInputAction::Epsilon),
1011	            InField => {
1012	                if self.delimiter == c {
1013	                    (EndFieldDelim, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1014	                } else if self.term.equals(c) {
1015	                    (EndFieldTerm, NfaInputAction::Epsilon)
1016	                } else {
1017	                    (InField, NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput)
1018	                }
1019	            }
1020	            InQuotedField => {
1021	                if self.quoting && self.quote == c {
1022	                    (InDoubleEscapedQuote, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1023	                } else if self.quoting && self.escape == Some(c) {
1024	                    (InEscapedQuote, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1025	                } else {
1026	                    (InQuotedField, NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput)
1027	                }
1028	            }
1029	            InEscapedQuote => (InQuotedField, NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput),
1030	            InDoubleEscapedQuote => {
1031	                if self.quoting && self.double_quote && self.quote == c {
1032	                    (InQuotedField, NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput)
1033	                } else if self.delimiter == c {
1034	                    (EndFieldDelim, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1035	                } else if self.term.equals(c) {
1036	                    (EndFieldTerm, NfaInputAction::Epsilon)
1037	                } else {
1038	                    (InField, NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput)
1039	                }
1040	            }
1041	            InComment => {
1042	                if b'\n' == c {
1043	                    (StartRecord, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1044	                } else {
1045	                    (InComment, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1046	                }
1047	            }
1048	            InRecordTerm => {
1049	                if self.term.is_crlf() && b'\r' == c {
1050	                    (CRLF, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1051	                } else {
1052	                    (EndRecord, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1053	                }
1054	            }
1055	            CRLF => {
1056	                if b'\n' == c {
1057	                    (StartRecord, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1058	                } else {
1059	                    (StartRecord, NfaInputAction::Epsilon)
1060	                }
1061	            }
1062	        }
1063	    }
1064	}

1066	/// The number of slots in the DFA transition table.
1067	///
1068	/// This number is computed by multiplying the maximum number of transition
1069	/// classes (7) by the total number of NFA states that are used in the DFA
1070	/// (10).
1071	///
1072	/// The number of transition classes is determined by an equivalence class of
1073	/// bytes, where every byte in the same equivalence classes is
1074	/// indistinguishable from any other byte with respect to the DFA. For example,
1075	/// if neither `a` nor `b` are specifed as a delimiter/quote/terminator/escape,
1076	/// then the DFA will never discriminate between `a` or `b`, so they can
1077	/// effectively be treated as identical. This reduces storage space
1078	/// substantially.
1079	///
1080	/// The total number of NFA states (13) is greater than the total number of
1081	/// NFA states that are in the DFA. In particular, any NFA state that can only
1082	/// be reached by epsilon transitions will never have explicit usage in the
1083	/// DFA.
1084	const TRANS_CLASSES: usize = 7;
1085	const DFA_STATES: usize = 10;
1086	const TRANS_SIZE: usize = TRANS_CLASSES * DFA_STATES;
1087	
1088	/// The number of possible transition classes. (See the comment on `TRANS_SIZE`
1089	/// for more details.)
1090	const CLASS_SIZE: usize = 256;
1091	
1092	/// A representation of a DFA.
1093	///
1094	/// For the most part, this is a transition table, but various optimizations
1095	/// have been applied to reduce its memory footprint.
1096	struct Dfa {
1097	    /// The core transition table. Each row corresponds to the transitions for
1098	    /// each input equivalence class. (Input bytes are mapped to their
1099	    /// corresponding equivalence class with the `classes` map.)
1100	    ///
1101	    /// DFA states are represented as an index corresponding to the start of
1102	    /// its row in this table.
1103	    trans: [DfaState; TRANS_SIZE],
1104	    /// A table with the same layout as `trans`, except its values indicate
1105	    /// whether a particular `(state, equivalence class)` pair should emit an
1106	    /// output byte.
1107	    has_output: [bool; TRANS_SIZE],
1108	    /// A map from input byte to equivalence class.
1109	    ///
1110	    /// This is responsible for reducing the effective alphabet size from
1111	    /// 256 to `TRANS_CLASSES`.
1112	    classes: DfaClasses,
1113	    /// The DFA state corresponding to being inside an unquoted field.
1114	    in_field: DfaState,
1115	    /// The DFA state corresponding to being inside an quoted field.
1116	    in_quoted: DfaState,
1117	    /// The minimum DFA state that indicates a field has been parsed. All DFA
1118	    /// states greater than this are also final-field states.
1119	    final_field: DfaState,
1120	    /// The minimum DFA state that indicates a record has been parsed. All DFA
1121	    /// states greater than this are also final-record states.
1122	    final_record: DfaState,
1123	}
1124	
1125	impl Dfa {
1126	    fn new() -> Dfa {
1127	        Dfa {
1128	            trans: [DfaState(0); TRANS_SIZE],
1129	            has_output: [false; TRANS_SIZE],
1130	            classes: DfaClasses::new(),
1131	            in_field: DfaState(0),
1132	            in_quoted: DfaState(0),
1133	            final_field: DfaState(0),
1134	            final_record: DfaState(0),
1135	        }
1136	    }

1138	    fn new_state(&self, nfa_state: NfaState) -> DfaState {
1139	        let nclasses = self.classes.num_classes() as u8;
1140	        let idx = (nfa_state as u8).checked_mul(nclasses).unwrap();
1141	        DfaState(idx)
1142	    }

1144	    fn new_state_final_end(&self) -> DfaState {
1145	        self.new_state(NfaState::StartRecord)
1146	    }

1153	        let cls = self.classes.classes[c as usize];
1154	        let idx = state.0 as usize + cls as usize;

1158	    fn set(&mut self, from: DfaState, c: u8, to: DfaState, output: bool) {
1159	        let cls = self.classes.classes[c as usize];
1160	        let idx = from.0 as usize + cls as usize;
1161	        self.trans[idx] = to;
1162	        self.has_output[idx] = output;
1163	    }

1166	        self.in_field = self.new_state(NfaState::InField);
1167	        self.in_quoted = self.new_state(NfaState::InQuotedField);
1168	        self.final_field = self.new_state(NfaState::EndFieldDelim);
1169	        self.final_record = self.new_state(NfaState::EndRecord);
1170	    }

1172	    fn new_read_field_result(
1173	        &self,
1174	        state: DfaState,
1175	        is_final_trans: bool,
1176	        inpdone: bool,
1177	        outdone: bool,
1178	    ) -> ReadFieldResult {
1179	        if state >= self.final_record {
1180	            ReadFieldResult::Field { record_end: true }
1181	        } else if state == self.final_field {
1182	            ReadFieldResult::Field { record_end: false }
1183	        } else if is_final_trans && state.is_start() {
1184	            ReadFieldResult::End
1185	        } else {
1186	            debug_assert!(state < self.final_field);
1187	            if !inpdone && outdone {
1188	                ReadFieldResult::OutputFull
1189	            } else {
1190	                ReadFieldResult::InputEmpty
1191	            }
1192	        }
1193	    }

1196	        &self,
1197	        state: DfaState,
1198	        is_final_trans: bool,
1199	        inpdone: bool,
1200	        outdone: bool,
1201	        endsdone: bool,
1202	    ) -> ReadRecordResult {
1203	        if state >= self.final_record {

1205	        } else if is_final_trans && state.is_start() {
1206	            ReadRecordResult::End
1207	        } else {
1208	            debug_assert!(state < self.final_record);
1209	            if !inpdone && outdone {
1210	                ReadRecordResult::OutputFull
1211	            } else if !inpdone && endsdone {
1212	                ReadRecordResult::OutputEndsFull
1213	            } else {
1214	                ReadRecordResult::InputEmpty
1215	            }
1216	        }
1217	    }

1220	/// A map from input byte to equivalence class.
1221	struct DfaClasses {
1222	    classes: [u8; CLASS_SIZE],
1223	    next_class: usize,
1224	}
1225	
1226	impl DfaClasses {
1227	    fn new() -> DfaClasses {
1228	        DfaClasses { classes: [0; CLASS_SIZE], next_class: 1 }
1229	    }
1230	
1231	    fn add(&mut self, b: u8) {
1232	        if self.next_class > CLASS_SIZE {
1233	            panic!("added too many classes")
1234	        }
1235	        self.classes[b as usize] = self.next_class as u8;
1236	        self.next_class += 1;
1237	    }

1243	    /// Scan and copy the input bytes to the output buffer quickly.
1244	    ///
1245	    /// This assumes that the current state of the DFA is either `InField` or
1246	    /// `InQuotedField`. In this case, all bytes corresponding to the first
1247	    /// equivalence class (i.e., not a delimiter/quote/escape/etc.) are
1248	    /// guaranteed to never result in a state transition out of the current
1249	    /// state. This function takes advantage of that copies every byte from
1250	    /// `input` in the first equivalence class to `output`. Once a byte is seen
1251	    /// outside the first equivalence class, we quit and should fall back to
1252	    /// the main DFA loop.
1253	    #[inline(always)]
1254	    fn scan_and_copy(
1255	        &self,
1256	        input: &[u8],
1257	        nin: &mut usize,
1258	        output: &mut [u8],
1259	        nout: &mut usize,
1260	    ) {
1261	        while *nin < input.len()
1262	            && *nout < output.len()
1263	            && self.classes[input[*nin] as usize] == 0
1264	        {
1265	            output[*nout] = input[*nin];
1266	            *nin += 1;
1267	            *nout += 1;
1268	        }
1269	    }
1270	}

1279	struct DfaState(u8);

1400	        let mut field = [0u8; 10];
1401	        let mut csv = Csv::new();
1402	        let mut row = Row::new();
1403	        let mut outpos = 0;
1404	        loop {
1405	            let (res, nin, nout) = rdr.read_field(data, &mut field[outpos..]);
1406	            data = &data[nin..];
1407	            outpos += nout;
1408	
1409	            match res {
1410	                ReadFieldResult::InputEmpty => {
1411	                    if !data.is_empty() {
1412	                        panic!("missing input data")
1413	                    }
1414	                }
1415	                ReadFieldResult::OutputFull => panic!("field too large"),
1416	                ReadFieldResult::Field { record_end } => {
1417	                    let s = str::from_utf8(&field[..outpos]).unwrap();
1418	                    row.push(Field::from(s).unwrap());
1419	                    outpos = 0;
1420	                    if record_end {
1421	                        csv.push(row);

1899	
1900	        // Without reseting the parser state, the reader will remember that
1901	        // we're in a quoted field, and therefore interpret the leading double
1902	        // quotes below as a single quote and the trailing quote as a matching
1903	        // terminator. With the reset, however, the parser forgets the quoted
1904	        // field and treats the leading double quotes as a syntax quirk and
1905	        // drops them, in addition to hanging on to the trailing unmatched
1906	        // quote. (Matches Python's behavior.)
1907	        rdr.reset();
1908	
1909	        assert_read!(rdr, b("\"\"bar\""), out, 6, 4, InputEmpty);
1910	        assert_eq!(&out[..4], b("bar\""));
1911	    }

I've found the upstream rust-csv has fixed the BOM streaming issue, and the current task is based on the 0.1.11/0.1.13 snapshot of csv-core. I decided not to strictly align with upstream's implementation, and designed a BOM detection solution using a local stack buffer to hold combined data for preprocessing each input feed. I'm now finalizing the specific algorithm details.

I've ruled out the more complex two-buffer solution, confirming the local stack buffer approach is simpler, and verified that the maximum size of combined preprocessed data is 2 plus the length of new input.

I've finalized the specific preprocessing algorithm for entry calls, and verified that the lifetime design of the corresponding public function is logically compliant. The algorithm first handles cached BOM prefix data, then performs BOM matching scanning on the concatenation of the cached prefix and new input bytes. If a complete BOM is detected, only the new bytes required to form the full BOM will be consumed from the input, with all other logic strictly following the confirmed processing rules.

I've clarified the processing logic for two scenarios under BOM checking mode: when a complete BOM is detected, only the new bytes needed to form the full BOM are consumed, with all remaining logic following the specified rules. When a BOM mismatch is found, BOM checking is disabled, the stored prefix and all new input are combined for subsequent processing, and all input bytes are marked as consumable.

I've confirmed that when BOM checking is pending and all new bytes are withheld, we must not trigger the final transition logic of the parser to avoid premature end-of-file reporting or empty field generation, as required by the task.

content.text:
All requirements are implemented and verified. Here's a summary of the work.

## What was wrong

`csv-core` stripped a UTF-8 BOM with a single non-streaming check (`strip_utf8_bom`): it only worked when all three bytes `EF BB BF` arrived in one call, before any read. If the marker was split across reads (e.g. byte-at-a-time through a 1-byte buffer), it was kept as data instead of removed — so chunked reads and whole-buffer reads produced different fields/headers/records.

## Changes

**`csv-core/src/reader.rs`**
- Replaced the one-shot check with a small streaming prefix matcher driven from `read_field`/`read_record`:
  - `bom_len` retains bytes matching a prefix of `EF BB BF` while the signature is undecided; the third matching byte confirms and strips it; any mismatch (or end of input after only `EF`/`EF BB`) releases the retained bytes verbatim into a 3-byte staging area (`bom_data`) that is replayed to the parser in order, compacting as space allows.
  - Retained/stripped bytes count as consumed by the call that actually received them; field-end positions never count the removed marker.
  - A chunk containing exactly the complete BOM returns `InputEmpty` (never a premature `End` or an empty field); end is still signaled only by an empty input. BOM-only and empty files yield no records.
  - Works with 1-byte output buffers, 1-slot end buffers, and occasionally-empty buffers, for both by-field and by-record reads; NFA and DFA share the path.
- `reset()` clears the pending prefix and re-enables detection; added `set_bom_checking(bool)` (only new public API) so seek-style callers can disable it at non-zero offsets.
- Fixed a latent pre-existing NFA `read_record` bug found while testing parity: it indexed the output at absolute `output_pos` into an already-sliced buffer (corrupting data with 1-byte fragments); it now uses relative offsets like the DFA.
- Stays `#![no_std]` (only core slice ops).

**`src/reader.rs`**: `seek`/`seek_raw` call `core.set_bom_checking(pos.byte() == 0)` after reset — BOM stripped only at file offset 0; same bytes at a later record kept. Byte positions remain in original-file coordinates (stripped bytes still count toward `nin`), so the first record is at 0 and later offsets include +3. No public entry points or index-format changes.

## Tests (all pass: 312 tests + doctests)

- `csv-core/tests/bom.rs` (13): differential driver over every chunk size and 1-byte/empty buffers for NFA & DFA; 1+1+1 / 1+2 / 2+1 splits; BOM-only first chunk; BOM-only/empty files; partial-signature and dangling-prefix preservation; explicit consumption/end accounting; empty-buffer at prefix release; later BOM bytes kept; reset.
- `tests/bom.rs` (9): headers + Serde (`name=甲, value=7`), no-headers two records, raw `EF BB,x` / `ok,y` bytes, StringRecord UTF-8 error at field 0 offset 0 stable across chunking, positions (+3), seek to non-zero vs 0, NFA/DFA parity, across buffer capacities 1–8192.
- `csv-index/tests/bom.rs` (2): `RandomAccessSimple` create/reopen, offsets 0/9/13/20, positional reads match sequential including a later U+FEFF-leading record.

`cargo fmt --check` is clean; clippy reports only pre-existing warnings; examples build. I did not commit — let me know if you'd like that.
